items.topic: Therapeutic communication — using silence gives the client time to think and process
items.stem: A client pauses after saying, “I’m not sure I can talk about this yet.” Which nurse action best uses silence as a therapeutic communication technique?

options.text: Remain quiet and present, allowing the client time to think and break the silence when ready
Immediately fill the pause with advice about what the client should feel
Change the subject to unit visiting hours to lighten the mood
Say, “Don’t worry—everything will be fine,” and leave the room

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax Fundamentals: using silence allows the patient time to think and process; nurses should respectfully let the patient break the silence. Open RN Fundamentals: providing silence gives clients time to process, self-reflect, and broach a new topic; the nurse may use nonverbal cues but does not rush to speak.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Filling silence with advice interrupts processing and can be nontherapeutic.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Changing the subject is a nontherapeutic barrier.
rationales.D: Incorrect. False reassurance and leaving abandon therapeutic presence.

items.stem: After a client discloses a painful experience and then falls silent, indicate whether each nurse behaviour is Indicated (therapeutic silence/presence) or Not indicated (nontherapeutic barrier).

items.topic: Infant burping — gently pat/rub back during and after feeds to release trapped air
items.stem: Parents ask how to burp their newborn who fusses with gas during feeds. Which teaching is correct?

options.text: During and after feeding, hold the infant in a supported burping position and gently pat or rub the back to help release swallowed air
Pound firmly between the shoulder blades for several minutes every time, even if the baby is comfortable
Never burp bottle-fed or breastfed infants because burping always causes injury
Lay the infant completely flat and shake the torso to move air out of the stomach

rationales.A: Correct. OpenStax: burping removes trapped air; use shoulder/lap positions and gently rub or pat the back; breastfed often between breasts and at end; bottle-fed as needed during/after. MedlinePlus: burp several times during and after feeding with upright support and gentle patting.
rationales.B: Incorrect. OpenStax: do not pound harder—this can cause injury and does not improve burping.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Both breastfed and bottle-fed infants may swallow air and benefit from burping.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Supported upright/lap burping positions are taught; shaking is unsafe.

items.jurisdiction_note: Health Canada and Canadian Cancer Society SPF 30+ guidance (stricter than some US SPF 15 minima)
items.topic: Canada sun safety — broad-spectrum water-resistant sunscreen SPF 30+; reapply about every 2 hours
items.stem: A community nurse in Canada teaches outdoor workers about sunscreen. Which instruction matches Canadian public-health guidance?

options.text: Use a broad-spectrum, water-resistant sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher and reapply at least every 2 hours (sooner if sweating/swimming)
Any lip balm without SPF fully replaces sunscreen for the face and body
Apply sunscreen once each spring and never reapply during outdoor work
Indoor tanning beds are a healthy way to build a protective base tan before summer

rationales.A: Correct. Health Canada: broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher; apply ≥15 minutes before sun; reapply at least every 2 hours and after sweating/swimming. Canadian Cancer Society: broad-spectrum SPF 30+; reapply every 2 hours or after sweating/swimming; use with shade/clothing/hats.
rationales.B: Incorrect. SPF lip balm protects lips but does not replace full-body sunscreen.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Reapplication at least every 2 hours during exposure is required.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Health Canada: avoid tanning equipment; no healthy tan; increases melanoma risk.

items.topic: Hand-foot-and-mouth disease — supportive care; antibiotics do not shorten the viral illness
items.stem: Parents of a toddler with hand, foot, and mouth disease ask for antibiotics “to clear it faster.” Which nurse response is best?

options.text: Antibiotics will not make this viral illness go away faster; focus on comfort, fluids, and fever/pain relief as directed, and hand hygiene to limit spread
Start leftover amoxicillin from a sibling’s ear infection today
Antibiotics are required for every child with HFMD to prevent lifelong carriage
Give aspirin every 4 hours until the rash disappears

rationales.A: Correct. CPS: no treatment for the infection; antibiotics won’t help it go away faster; comfort, fluids, acetaminophen/ibuprofen for mouth-sore pain; handwashing. CDC: usually get better in 7–10 days with minimal/no medical treatment; manage pain/fever; never give aspirin to children.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Leftover antibiotics are inappropriate for this viral illness and unsafe.
rationales.C: Incorrect. HFMD is viral; antibiotics are not routinely indicated.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CDC: never give aspirin to children (Reye risk context for viral illness).

items.topic: TeamSTEPPS DESC script — constructive approach for interpersonal/hostile conflict
items.stem: A colleague repeatedly humiliates a nurse in front of clients. Which TeamSTEPPS tool is most appropriate to manage this interpersonal conflict constructively?

options.text: Use the DESC script (Describe, Express, Suggest, Consequences) in a private, respectful conversation focused on win-win resolution
Ignore the behaviour indefinitely because conflict tools are only for medication orders
Yell the same insults back at the colleague in the hallway to “even the score”
Post the colleague’s name and complaints on social media for public shaming

rationales.A: Correct. AHRQ TeamSTEPPS DESC tool: constructive approach for managing/resolving conflict, especially interpersonal/hostile or harassing behaviours risking harm; use private location and “I” statements. CUSP/TeamSTEPPS notes: DESC = Describe, Express, Suggest, Consequences.
rationales.B: Incorrect. DESC is intended for conflict management, including interpersonal conflict affecting safety/teamwork.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Retaliatory public confrontation is not DESC and harms patients/team.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Public shaming is unprofessional and not a TeamSTEPPS conflict tool.

items.jurisdiction_note: Ontario CNO Discontinuing or Declining to Provide Care + Code of Conduct 3.13
items.topic: CNO — do not abandon clients; arrange alternative/replacement services when discontinuing care
items.stem: An Ontario nurse plans to discontinue nursing services for a client who still needs care. Which action best meets CNO accountabilities?

options.text: Arrange timely alternative or replacement services, or give the client a reasonable opportunity to arrange them—do not abandon the client
Stop all care immediately without notice because the nurse is annoyed with the client
Walk away mid-shift without communicating with the client, team, or employer
Refuse to explore any options and leave the client without access to ongoing care

rationales.A: Correct. CNO Discontinuing or Declining to Provide Care: nurses cannot abandon/neglect clients; ensure ongoing access to care; discontinue only after other options explored. Code of Conduct 3.13: arrange timely alternative/replacement services or provide reasonable opportunity to arrange them. Professional misconduct regulation also addresses discontinuation without alternatives.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Annoyance alone is not a basis to abandon needed services without alternatives.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Clear communication with client/team/employer is required.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Exploring options and ensuring access to care are required.

items.topic: NGN cloze — CNO discontinuing care requires alternatives or reasonable opportunity
items.stem: Complete the statement about Ontario nurses’ accountabilities when discontinuing nursing services.

ngn.template: Nurses must not {B1} clients; when discontinuing needed services they arrange {B2} or provide a {B3}.

B2.text: secret social-media posts about the client
immediate cessation with zero notice always
care only if the nurse likes the client

B3.text: reasonable opportunity for the client to arrange alternative services
guarantee that no other provider will ever be involved
plan to leave without any handover

rationales.B1a: Correct. CNO: nurses cannot abandon or neglect clients to whom they have a care commitment.
rationales.B1b: Incorrect. Documentation remains required; the blank concerns abandonment.
rationales.B1c: Incorrect. Communication is required, not prohibited.
rationales.B1d: Incorrect. Nurses must follow the Code; this is not what must be avoided.
rationales.B2a: Correct. Code 3.13: arrange timely alternative or replacement services.
rationales.B2b: Incorrect. Social-media posting of client information is prohibited.
rationales.B2c: Incorrect. Zero-notice cessation without alternatives risks abandonment.
rationales.B2d: Incorrect. Care decisions are not based on personal liking.
rationales.B3a: Correct. Provide a reasonable opportunity to arrange alternative services.
rationales.B3b: Incorrect. Alternative providers are part of safe transition.

items.topic: HFMD infection control — hand hygiene and stay home while symptomatic
items.client_needs_subcategory: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
items.stem: A daycare asks how to limit spread of hand, foot, and mouth disease. Which instruction is best?

options.text: Promote frequent handwashing with soap and water, clean/disinfect toys and surfaces, and keep symptomatic children home from daycare/school
Stop all handwashing because HFMD is not contagious
Encourage hugging and sharing drinks with children who have active mouth sores
Tell parents HFMD never spreads through saliva or stool

rationales.A: Correct. CDC: wash hands often, clean/disinfect surfaces, avoid close contact with infected persons. CPS: handwashing best prevention; wash toys/surfaces; children should stay home from school/child care if they have symptoms; spreads via saliva/stool.
rationales.B: Incorrect. HFMD is very contagious; hand hygiene is essential.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Avoid close contact/kissing/hugging while infectious; do not share fluids with mouth sores.
rationales.D: Incorrect. CPS/CDC: spreads through saliva/droplets and stool/contact with contaminated objects.
